about: A visit to the fire station

lines.text: Last Saturday, my scout group visited the fire station near our school.
A firefighter named Mr Hakim welcome us at the gate and showed us around.
lines.note: Tense: 'welcomed … and showed' — both verbs are in the past.

lines.text: First, we saw the three fire engine that the station uses every day.
Each engine carry enough water to fill a small swimming pool.
lines.note: Agreement: 'each engine' is one thing, so it is 'carries'.

lines.text: Mr Hakim then let us try on a helmet, which was heavier than
it looked. He explained that a firefighter must get dressed in under a minute.
When a alarm rings, the crew slide down the pole to save time.
lines.note: Article: 'alarm' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an alarm'.

lines.text: We also learnt how to use an extinguisher, and every scout were given a
lines.note: Agreement: 'every scout' takes a singular verb, so it is 'was'.

lines.text: turn. I aimed the hose bad at first and sprayed my own shoes.
lines.note: Word form: 'aimed' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'badly'.

lines.text: Before we left, Mr Hakim remind us never to leave a stove unattended.
lines.note: Tense: the visit is in the past, so it is 'reminded'.

lines.text: He also gave each of us two sticker with the emergency number on them.
I have stuck mine on the fridge at home.
